profiles.summary: Two execution clients that no cycle had read now carry new code on the paths the PoolManager uses. Erigon 3.8 replaced its jump destination scan with CPU-selected SSE4 and NEON kernels and added a per-frame cache in front of SLOAD, and Nethermind 2.2.2 keeps stack words in little-endian limbs and picks one of four SIMD jump destination kernels at run time. The erigon SSE4 kernel, run here on the PoolManager bytecode and 690,000 other byte strings, matches the scalar rule; the battery and targeted set match again on reth v2.11.0, geth v1.17.10 and a pocket gateway that rotates reth, geth and erigon backends.

deltas.delta: eth.api.pocket.network, which cycle 21 recorded as reth v2.11.0, now rotates per request between reth v2.10.1, reth v2.11.0, Geth v1.17.9 built with go1.25.14, erigon 3.8.1 (go1.27.3), erigon 3.8.2 (go1.27.2 and go1.27.4) and erigon 3.3.9 (go1.25.8). It serves eth_call with state override. The gas a call without a gas field receives takes four values (about 50 million, 500 million, 1 billion and 10 billion), so the backends run with different call caps.
deltas.source: rpc: web3_clientVersion and eth_call on https://eth.api.pocket.network, 2026-11-26 (research/network-risk/cycles/024/ethereum-reference.work/pin-battery.json, pin-targeted.json, slotcache-pocket.json)

deltas.delta: erigon v3.8.0 to v3.8.2 compute the jump destination bitmap with a branch-free SSSE3 and SSE4.1 assembly kernel on amd64 (execution/vm/analysis_amd64.s) and a NEON kernel on arm64 (analysis_arm64.s), chosen at start from the CPU flags, with a chunked scalar fallback (analysis.go). v3.7.0 has no such file. JUMP and JUMPI accept a destination only through this bitmap (contract.go validJumpdest), with no separate check of the byte.

erigon v3.8.1 and v3.8.2 pin github.com/holiman/uint256 at an untagged commit 087f4b32f234 of 2026-02-28 instead of v1.3.2, which geth v1.17.10 pins. Against v1.3.2 the commit rewrites Slt and Sgt as a test on the top limb, gives SDiv an explicit zero case and a sign test on the top bit, unrolls PutUint256 and WriteToSlice, and adds in-place helpers and MulDivOverflowRem. AddMod, MulMod and the division in mod.go are unchanged. Each rewritten function gives the specified result as read.

erigon v3.8.1 opExp adds fast paths for exponent 0 and 1 and base 0, 1 and 2 (2^e for e below 256, else 0). They match the specification. opSAR, opSHL and opSHR clamp shifts of 256 or more on the whole word.

Nethermind 2.2.2, the newest tag found, stores stack words in UInt256 limb order (least significant byte first) and rewrites ADD, SUB, the comparisons, BYTE, SIGNEXTEND, the shifts, SAR, ADDMOD, MULMOD and EXP on raw limbs. Its jump destination analysis picks an AVX-512 VBMI, AVX2, SSSE3 or AdvSimd kernel by CPU at run time, with a scalar fallback, and keeps a separate bitmap with EIP-7979 CALLDEST bytes. It links Nethermind.Numerics.Int256 1.11.0; the 2.3.0-rc tag links 1.15.0. No public mainnet endpoint names Nethermind, and clientdiversity.org puts it on about 43 percent of reporting validators.
reth main still reports 2.11.0 and pins evm2 7c9f3b6d, as in cycle 21. ruint has no release after 1.21.1; its Unreleased section is the one cycle 21 read. geth master reports 1.17.11-unstable.

profiles.summary: Erigon 3.8 holds the last two storage reads of each frame in a cache keyed by the stack word and an IntraBlockState read stamp. The source that defines when the stamp changes was not found. A probe that reads a slot, lets a nested frame write it, reverts a second nested write, and writes it through a delegatecall gave the right words on reth, geth and 250 calls to the rotating pocket gateway. Only one of those calls was pinned to erigon by both brackets.

deltas.delta: erigon v3.8.1 opSload (execution/vm/instructions.go:766-788) answers from a two-entry per-frame cache (frameSlots, interpreter.go:93-145) when the IntraBlockState ReadStamp equals the stamp stored with the entry. SSTORE goes to IntraBlockState.SetState with no direct touch of the cache. The cache turns itself off after eight misses without a hit.
EIP-8141 (frame transaction, scheduled for Hegota with no date) says clients discard TSTORE and TLOAD transient storage between frames.

profiles.summary: Nothing new for gas, the native asset or token contracts on Ethereum. The endpoints give a simulated call different gas caps, which changes only how much of a script a node can afford.

The L-487 shape (two balanceOf(PoolManager) reads around a storage clear, a value transfer and a transient write) on 95 precompiles, system contracts, staking, account abstraction, infrastructure and bridge contracts gives the same word twice for every target. When the value goes to the target itself, only WETH9 and the three EntryPoints raise the reading, by the 1 wei sent.

deltas.delta: eth_config on reth v2.11.0 reports the current fork as active since 1767747671 (2026-01-07) with fork id 0x07c9462e, a blob schedule of target 14 and max 21, P256VERIFY at 0x100, and no next fork.

profiles.summary: No mainnet fork is scheduled: eth_config has no next fork and the Glamsterdam table still lists Sepolia only. Hegota now considers EIP-7979 (CALLSUB, CALLDEST as a jump destination), EIP-8163 (EXTENSION 0xae) and EIP-8173, none of which changes how the PoolManager bytecode decodes. At block 26,498,431 the finalized head was 91 blocks back, and published Xatu data put the 2025 reorg rate at about 0.11 percent of slots.

deltas.delta: EIP-8081 lists as Considered for Hegota EIP-7979 call and return opcodes, EIP-8163 EXTENSION, EIP-5920 PAY, EIP-8298 SETCODEFROM and EIP-8360 TCREATE, and as Proposed EIP-8173 Foundations of EVM Control Flow. Only EIP-7805 FOCIL and EIP-8141 frames are Scheduled. No activation date is set.

EIP-7979 makes CALLDEST (0xBB) a valid JUMP and JUMPI destination. A linear decode of the PoolManager runtime, both the build of this checkout and the mainnet code, finds no 0xBB, 0xBC, 0xBF, 0xBD, 0xBE, 0xAE, 0xFC, 0xA7 or 0xF6 byte at an instruction boundary. The eight 0xBB bytes are all inside push data.

eth_getBlockByNumber on reth v2.11.0 at 2026-11-26: latest 26,498,431, safe 26,498,371, finalized 26,498,340 (about 18 minutes behind). The ethresear.ch analysis of Xatu data for January to August 2025 gives a reorg rate of 0.1121 percent after Pectra.

findings.title: Minority Ethereum execution clients run CPU-selected jump destination kernels and an erigon storage read cache that no public endpoint can be pinned to
findings.difference: Erigon 3.8 (about 3 percent of reporting validators) and Nethermind 2.2 (about 43 percent) compute the jump destination bitmap with SIMD kernels chosen from the CPU at start, so validators running one release on different hardware run different code for it. Erigon 3.8 also answers SLOAD from a two-entry per-frame cache whose invalidation rests on a read stamp of its state object. Geth and reth, which earlier cycles tested, do neither of the erigon changes. No public endpoint serves eth_call from Nethermind, and the only one that reaches erigon rotates its backend on every request.
findings.mechanism: Every branch of the PoolManager is a JUMP or JUMPI to one of its 610 JUMPDEST bytes. A kernel that dropped one of them would make that branch fail on the affected client. A kernel that marked a 0x5b byte inside push data would change nothing, because the PoolManager never jumps to a computed target taken from input. The storage cache matters at PoolManager.sol:196 and 202-206 and at 154-159: the frame reads slot0 for checkPoolInitialized, calls the hook, and reads slot0 and the liquidity again inside Pool.swap or Pool.modifyLiquidity. If the stamp did not change when a hook reentered the PoolManager and moved the price, or when a nested write was reverted, the outer frame would swap from the old price. The erigon SSE4 kernel and its scalar fallback were built here from the v3.8.1 source and matched an independent scalar rule on the PoolManager bytecode (build and mainnet code, 610 destinations), on all 192 prefix and suffix cuts of each, on 400,000 random strings and on 289,510 single-push strings; a one-byte change to the kernel's JUMPDEST constant gave 1.2 million mismatches, so the harness sees a fault. The NEON kernel and the four Nethermind kernels were not run. The cache probe gave the specified words on every answer.
findings.impact: None found. A fault in a client below one third of the stake makes its nodes reject canonical blocks; it does not change what the canonical chain records for pool funds. Nethermind is above one third, so a Nethermind fault on a PoolManager path would stall finality until fixed, and funds would wait without loss. Changing the recorded state needs a fault in clients holding two thirds of the stake.
findings.preconditions: A fault in one of the unrun kernels or in the read stamp logic, reached by a PoolManager path, on clients that together hold enough stake to matter. Nobody has to hold a role to send the transaction that reaches it, but the effect on funds needs the faulty client to dominate block production and attestation.
findings.mitigations: Run the Nethermind JumpDestinationAnalyzer kernels and the erigon NEON kernel against the PoolManager bytecode and the scalar rule. Read the erigon ReadStamp source. Operators with a choice can keep a geth or reth node beside an erigon or Nethermind validator.

sources.supports: erigon v3.8.1 jump destination kernel in SSSE3 and SSE4.1 assembly
per-frame two-entry SLOAD cache keyed by ReadStamp
jump validity read from the bitmap alone, cached by code hash
Nethermind selects AVX-512 VBMI, AVX2, SSSE3 or AdvSimd kernels at run time
execution client shares of reporting validators: Nethermind about 43 percent, geth 43, Besu 8, reth 3, erigon 3

cleared.check: The 99,985 vector battery and the 85,544 vector targeted set on reth v2.11.0 (publicnode), geth v1.17.10 go1.27.3 (nownodes) and the pocket gateway, every call bracketed by web3_clientVersion.
cleared.result: All 185,529 vectors gave the specified word on all three. publicnode was pinned to reth v2.11.0 on all 310 calls and nownodes to geth v1.17.10 on 300 of 310 (the rest were 429 answers to the bracket). On pocket, 119 of 310 calls had the same backend in both brackets: reth v2.10.1 77, reth v2.11.0 39, geth v1.17.9 go1.25.14 1, erigon 3.8.1 1 and erigon 3.8.2 go1.27.2 1. So reth v2.10.1 and the go1.25.14 geth build are newly covered, and erigon only by two batches of 600 vectors.

cleared.check: erigon v3.8.1 jump destination analysis: the SSE4 kernel (analysis_amd64.s, analysis_amd64.go) and the generic chunked scan (analysis.go), built locally from the tagged source with only the package name and the CPU flag test changed, against an independent scalar rule.
cleared.result: No mismatch in 689,896 cases: the PoolManager runtime of this checkout's build and of mainnet (24,009 bytes, 610 destinations each), 96 prefix and 96 suffix cuts of each, 400,000 random strings up to 300 bytes from four byte distributions, and every push opcode from 0x5f to 0x80 at every position of a run of JUMPDEST bytes of length 0 to 130. Bits past the code length stay clear. Replacing one JUMPDEST constant byte in the kernel gave 1,208,869 mismatches. The signed test int8(op) < int8(PUSH1) in the generic scan treats 0x80 to 0xff as one-byte instructions, which is right. v3.8.2 has byte-identical analysis files.

cleared.check: erigon v3.8.1 instruction handlers used by src/libraries: ADD, SUB, MUL, DIV, SDIV, MOD, SMOD, EXP, SIGNEXTEND, LT, GT, SLT, SGT, EQ, ISZERO, BYTE, ADDMOD, MULMOD, SHL, SHR, SAR, KECCAK256, CALLDATALOAD, JUMP, JUMPI, and the uint256 commit 087f4b32f234 behind them.
cleared.result: Each handler takes its operands in the specified order and calls the library, with clamps for shifts of 256 or more on the whole word and an overflow test for CALLDATALOAD offsets. The new library code (top-limb Slt and Sgt, SDiv zero case and sign test, unrolled byte output) gives the specified result for all sign and zero cases as read. The battery's SLT, SGT, SDIV and MULDIV512 vectors exercise these functions.

cleared.check: Nethermind 2.2.2 handlers for ADD, SUB, LT, GT, SLT, SGT, DIV, SDIV, MOD, SMOD, EXP, ADDMOD, MULMOD, SHL, SHR, SAR, BYTE, SIGNEXTEND, ISZERO, NOT and CLZ on the little-endian limb stack.
cleared.result: Operand order matches the specification in each (the popped slot above the new top is the first operand). SDIV returns the minimum value for the minimum value divided by -1 and 0 for a zero divisor, MOD and SMOD return 0 for divisors 0 and 1, ADDMOD and MULMOD return 0 for a zero modulus, shifts of 256 or more give 0 or the sign fill, BYTE reads slot byte 31 - i for i below 32 and 0 otherwise, and SIGNEXTEND extends from bit 8i+7 for i below 31 and leaves the word alone otherwise. The Int256 library routines behind DIV, SDIV, MOD, SMOD, MULMOD and EXP were not read.

cleared.check: A per-frame storage read cache that returns a stale slot after a nested frame writes it, after a nested write is reverted, or after a delegatecall writes it: the pattern of PoolManager.sol:196 to 206, where the swap frame reads slot0, a hook may reenter, and Pool.swap reads slot0 again.
cleared.result: The probe contract reads slot 1 (prestate 5) twice and slot 2 once, calls itself to write 7, reads 7, calls itself to write 9 and revert, reads 7, delegatecalls code that writes 11, reads 11, writes 13 and reads 13. All answers were [5, 7, 7, 11, 13]: 3 of 3 on reth v2.11.0, 2 of 2 on geth v1.17.10 and 250 of 250 on the pocket gateway, whose brackets named an erigon build 35 times. Only one call had erigon in both brackets (3.8.2), so this is weak evidence for erigon, and the ReadStamp source was not found.

cleared.check: Lead L-487 added shape: two staticcalls of X.balanceOf(PoolManager) from a stub at the PoolManager address, with a clear of storage slot 0, a 1 wei value call and a transient write between them. Shape A sends the wei to an unrelated codeless account, shape B to X with empty calldata. 95 targets from the cycle 8 list: 18 precompiles, 7 system addresses, WETH9, 25 staking contracts, 15 account abstraction and infrastructure contracts, 29 bridge contracts.
cleared.result: Shape A: every target gave the same success flag, return size and word on both reads. Shape B: only WETH9 and EntryPoints 0.6, 0.7 and 0.8 raised the reading, each by exactly the 1 wei sent, which is the mirrored-ledger case cycle 3 recorded; the caller of such a take is debited the native amount first (P1). stETH reported no change for 1 wei (share rounding). No ledger moved without a payment.
cleared.source: research/network-risk/cycles/024/ethereum-reference.work/l487.py, l487.json (reth v2.11.0 at the block recorded in the file)

cleared.check: Hegota candidates that change control flow or opcode bytes: EIP-7979 (CALLSUB 0xBC, CALLDEST 0xBB as a valid jump destination, RETURNSUB 0xBF), EIP-8163 (EXTENSION 0xae), EIP-5920 (PAY 0xfc), EIP-8298 and EIP-8360, against the PoolManager runtime.
cleared.result: None of these bytes, nor 0xBD, 0xBE, 0xA7 or 0xF6, sits at an instruction boundary of the build or of the mainnet code, so no new jump destination appears and no instruction changes meaning. EIP-8163 requires that EXTENSION leave jump destination analysis unchanged. PAY into the PoolManager would add ETH that no account can book, because native settlement credits msg.value only (src/PoolManager.sol:352-354).

cleared.check: Lead L-1047: what an ordinary account can undo or reorder around another account's PoolManager transaction, using the entry points that need no unlock.
cleared.result: Ordering cannot move a credit. sync writes only transient slots of the current transaction (src/libraries/CurrencyReserves.sol:23-30, src/PoolManager.sol:279-288), which EIP-1153 clears at the end of the transaction, so a sync in an inserted transaction is gone before the victim's starts. settle compares the balance with what the victim's own sync recorded inside its own transaction (src/PoolManager.sol:349-364), so tokens sent to the PoolManager by another transaction before that sync are part of the recorded reserves and are credited to no one. ERC-6909 transfer and transferFrom move only the caller's claims or allowances given to it (src/ERC6909.sol:25-45). extsload and exttload are views. initialize only succeeds on a pool with no price (src/libraries/Pool.sol:101), so a front-run can choose the starting price of a pool nobody has created; modifyLiquidity takes no price bound (src/types/PoolOperation.sol:8-16), so a direct caller without a slippage check of its own would add at that price. That is the same on every network and is the job of the caller's router. Inside one block, a builder or searcher can sandwich swaps, which the swapper bounds with sqrtPriceLimitX96. Reorgs on mainnet are one block deep in the 2025 data (about 0.11 percent of slots) and blocks finalize about 18 minutes behind the head; a reorg drops or reorders whole transactions and cannot split one settlement.

cleared.check: Upcoming forks within six months, assumed shipped the day after.
cleared.result: eth_config on reth v2.11.0 shows no next fork, and EIP-7773 still lists Sepolia (2026-10-06) only. The Glamsterdam scheduled list is the 20 EIPs cycles 14, 17 and 21 cleared; the Hegota scheduled list is still FOCIL and EIP-8141. EIP-8141 now states that transient storage is discarded between frames, so a sync or an unlock flag left by one frame cannot reach a native settle in another (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288, 356). Nothing an ordinary account could do the day after changes a PoolManager result.

leads.question: Do the four Nethermind 2.2.2 jump destination kernels (Vector512 with AVX-512 VBMI, Vector256, SSSE3, AdvSimd) give the scalar bitmap on the PoolManager runtime, its prefix and suffix cuts and the random and single-push sets of cycles/024/ethereum-reference.work/jdtest?
leads.why: Nethermind runs on about 43 percent of reporting validators, so a dropped destination on a PoolManager branch would stall finality. No public endpoint serves Nethermind and no .NET runtime is installed here, so the kernels were only read.

leads.question: Where does erigon v3.8.1 define IntraBlockState.ReadStamp (execution/state), and does the stamp change on every SetState of any frame, on every journal revert and on SELFDESTRUCT or create into an address with storage?
leads.why: The per-frame SLOAD cache returns a stored word whenever the stamp is unchanged. A missing bump on a nested write would let an outer PoolManager frame swap from a price a hook already moved (src/PoolManager.sol:196-206). The probe passed but only one call was pinned to erigon.

leads.question: Does the erigon v3.8.1 NEON jump destination kernel (execution/vm/analysis_arm64.s) give the scalar bitmap on the jdtest inputs when run on arm64 or under emulation?
leads.why: arm64 validators run that kernel instead of the SSE4 one that was tested here.

leadResults.answer: For Ethereum: no fork after Fusaka and its blob parameter forks has a mainnet date. eth_config on reth v2.11.0 lists no next fork and EIP-7773 lists Sepolia only. Glamsterdam's opcode changes (EIP-7843, EIP-8024) were cleared for the bytecode in cycle 14 and its gas changes in cycles 8 and 17; none changes an opcode result, return data or the 63/64 rule, and the call sites forward gas() (src/types/Currency.sol:48, 73; src/libraries/Hooks.sol:134). Which OP Stack and Nitro releases carry these rules dormant is outside this unit and was not checked.

For Ethereum: Glamsterdam has no mainnet date, and the PoolManager runtime has no 0x4b, 0xe6, 0xe7 or 0xe8 byte at an instruction boundary (cycle 14, rechecked this cycle together with the Hegota bytes 0xBB, 0xBC, 0xBF, 0xAE, 0xFC). Nethermind 2.2.2 implements EIP-8024 immediates only in the separate jump-and-call bitmap, for code that holds CALLDEST bytes. The other networks listed in the lead are outside this unit.

Glamsterdam still has no mainnet date (eth_config and EIP-7773 on 2026-11-26). Both parts of the lead have been read: geth v1.17.9 in cycle 17 and reth's access list executor in cycle 21, which clears transient storage after each transaction, commits in block order and checks the rebuilt list against the header. Erigon 3.8 and Nethermind also carry access list execution, and erigon's per-frame storage cache is the new item; it is a lead of this cycle.

Active fork: the fork active since 2026-01-07 (eth_config fork id 0x07c9462e on reth v2.11.0), with no next fork. Glamsterdam has no mainnet date. The only scheduled multi-frame transaction type is EIP-8141 in Hegota, and its text now says transient storage is discarded between frames, so one party's leftover sync cannot reach another party's native settle (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288, 356). The sixteen shape sweep on Ethereum was run in cycle 8 (L-209); this cycle added the two-read shape of L-487 on the same 95 targets.

Ethereum part only. With a storage clear, a 1 wei transfer to an unrelated account and a transient write between two balanceOf(PoolManager) reads, all 95 targets answered the same word twice. When the wei went to the target itself, only WETH9 and the three EntryPoints rose, by exactly 1 wei, the known mirrored-ledger case. Monad and MegaETH were not run in this unit.

No entry point that needs no unlock lets an inserted transaction change another account's credit: sync state is transient and per transaction, settle measures from the victim's own sync, ERC-6909 transfers move only the caller's claims, and extsload is a view (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288, 349-364; src/ERC6909.sol:25-45). Front-running initialize picks the price of a pool nobody has created, and a caller adding liquidity without its own slippage check takes that price on every network. Mainnet reorgs are one block deep at about 0.11 percent of slots (ethresear.ch, 2025 data), finality is about 18 minutes behind the head, and a reorg drops or reorders whole transactions.
